note.note:
H&P – Super Detailed Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
Young woman with 2-day history of mid-lower abdominal pain, urinary frequency, and pink-tinged urine was assessed via tele-consult; uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection (cystitis) considered most likely and a 3-day oral antibiotic course was prescribed with safety-net advice.

History:
• Presenting complaint: “Pain in my lower tummy” for 2 days.  
• Location: Central/ suprapubic.  
• Character/progression: Persistent over 48 h; no prior similar episodes.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Feels “hot and sweaty,” measured home temperature 37 °C (only reading).  
  – Mild nausea; no vomiting.  
  – Increased urinary frequency; no dysuria.  
  – Slight pink discoloration of urine noted once (gross hematuria).  
  – Increased thirst.  
  – Constipation last week, currently resolved; normal bowel action 2 h prior to call; no diarrhoea.  
  – Denies back/flank pain, acid reflux, vaginal discharge, inter-menstrual or post-coital bleeding, shivering/rigors.  
• Exacerbating / relieving factors: none reported.  
• Systems review (pertinent negatives): No chest pain, shortness of breath, upper-abdominal pain, headache, or recent travel.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical conditions reported.  
• Prior contraceptive implant, removed 1 year ago.  
• No prior urinary problems.

Medications / Allergies:
• Regular medications: none.  
• OTC medications: none.  
• Allergy: Amoxicillin (reaction details not documented).

Social History:
• Lives with parents.  
• Smoking: never.  
• Alcohol: about 1 beer on 4 days per week.  
• No recent overseas travel.

Family History:
• Mother – breast cancer (treated early, outcome good).  
• No other familial conditions mentioned.

Physical Examination:
• Remote consult; no in-person examination performed.  
• Reported vitals: self-checked temperature 37 °C.  
• No other exam findings recorded.

Investigations:
• None performed during consultation; no urine dipstick, labs, or imaging available.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Suspected acute uncomplicated cystitis  
  – Assessment: Suprapubic pain, urinary frequency, visible hematuria, low-grade/absent fever, no flank pain → consistent with lower UTI.  
  – Plan:  
    • Empiric antibiotic (specific agent not documented) prescribed: “twice daily for 3 days.”  
    • Encourage adequate oral hydration.  
    • Safety-net: If pain worsens, temperature rises, develops back/flank pain, or new/ recurrent symptoms, contact service urgently for possible face-to-face review.  
    • Pharmacy on file to dispense medication.

Issue 2: Hematuria – monitor  
  – Assessment: Likely secondary to cystitis; alternative causes (urolithiasis, trauma) less likely but considered.  
  – Plan: Reassess if macroscopic hematuria persists after infection treatment; may require urine analysis and imaging.

Issue 3: Abdominal pain – other causes (appendicitis, gynae, stone)  
  – Assessment: Atypical features for appendicitis/stone/PID but discussed.  
  – Plan: Patient advised to seek immediate care if pain localises, intensifies, or systemic symptoms develop.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Acute uncomplicated cystitis – High likelihood: suprapubic pain, frequency, gross hematuria, minimal systemic signs, female of reproductive age.  
2. Urolithiasis – Moderate likelihood: hematuria and pain could represent distal ureteric stone; absence of colicky flank pain makes less likely.  
3. Early appendicitis – Low-moderate likelihood: central abdominal pain and mild nausea could represent early stage; urinary findings argue against.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing but expected:  
  – Pregnancy status not documented.  
  – Abdominal and pelvic physical examination absent (tele-visit limitation).  
  – No urine dipstick or culture ordered; vitals limited to self-reported temperature.  
• Conflicts between transcript and DDx: none significant (both support cystitis despite absent dysuria).  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio with occasional brief misunderstandings; overall adequate.
